The seam in the back hits you halfway through your behind, which cuts your butt in half and will make it seem larger than it is. The seam should hit above or at the waistline to draw attention up and emphasize your waist, or the seam should taper down below to emphasize the shape of your behind. If a seam hits you at a vertical angle, it's much more flattering than at a horizontal, which cuts you off. The hem is irregular and the fabric hanging down is drawing attention away from your legs. You want the hem to hit you just above, on, or just below the knee. This goes for any type of skirt or dress, unless of course we are taking about a maxi which will hit on your ankles.
